Situations / Concordat Magus Dragon

What Is the Tessarine Concordat’s True Architect

The Tessarine Concordat is not a commercial empire. It is a hoard. Its true architect is a Magus Dragon who accumulates obligation — leverage over councils, trade routes, institutions, and inherited debt — rather than gold. The dragon has been building this for centuries and does not intend to reveal itself.

Key Actors

  • The Magus Dragon — true architect; the Concordat is its hoard; operates through Cosimo Verantio and the factor network
  • Cosimo Verantio — the public face the dragon wears when the hoard is threatened; white-bearded elderly factor; “the Principal” to most of the Concordat; his signature appears on the oldest and largest debt instruments; never attends meetings unless the hoard is directly threatened
  • Iacopo Fieschi — Tessarine Envoy to Calveno; holds leverage through six Houses’ trade debt; extending credit to holdout Houses with sweetened terms and no immediate conditions
  • Perrin Black-Jaw — affected by the Calveno council deadlock above the Warren
  • Jean-Claude Tabarnack — strong fit for the Port Tidefall salvage contract

The Hoard’s Structure

The Concordat’s factors are the dragon’s Circle, but they do not know they are a Circle. They believe they are maintaining an institution. In practice, every contract, vote, route dependency, and inherited obligation feeds a hoard made of leverage instead of gold.

Where other Magus Dragons accumulate scholars, this one accumulates obligation. Destroying gold would not hurt this dragon — invalidating debt, freeing councils from obligation, or making Tessarine paper unreliable would.

The Vault of the First Factor — a hidden depository beneath Concordat territory — holds collateral from the region’s earliest debtors. This is the nearest equivalent to a physical hoard.

Current Threads

  • Unusual money moving through Calveno’s broker network toward the Maw is connected to a Tessarine-commissioned salvage operation targeting the Red Lady wreck — public face is salvage financing; hidden stakes are the Pearl of Souls and Concordat intelligence that went down with the expedition. See Who Commissioned the Theft.
  • The Port Tidefall trade house holds salvage manifests for a current Shearwall Reef salvage contract — roughly 800 gp (40% share) available to a capable party.
  • Aldric Drave — the Concordat moved to keep the Pearl away from him before he could reach it.

If Ignored

The dragon continues consolidating obligation across Calveno and the Crown Islands. PC-adjacent councils and factions accumulate Concordat debt without knowing who ultimately holds it.

At-Table Reveal

Late-game Concordat play should reframe commerce as draconic hoarding without changing its texture. The contracts were always predatory. The reveal is that they were also treasure.

The Concordat’s factors are sincere — they genuinely believe they maintain an institution. The most effective way to wound the dragon is not to burn the trade houses — it is to make the debt unenforceable, the councils ungrateful, and the paper worthless.
